sections.summary: The capability is a documented reporting limitation: ad-level name and data from upgraded Smart+ campaigns are not reported to MMPs; it is not a setting or control.

claims.text: For upgraded Smart+ campaigns, the ad-level name and ad-level data are not reported to mobile measurement partners (MMPs).

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

conditions: Scope given by the packet: upgraded Smart+ campaigns; the packet makes no statement about other TikTok campaign types.

claims.text: This is a reporting-scope limitation (what MMPs receive), not a control, delivery setting, or optimisation option.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

conditions: Editorial scoping based on the packet's reporting context; the packet is silent on delivery or controls.

sections.summary: The evidence explains the limitation causally as a mismatch between the number of reporting levels in upgraded Smart+ and what MMPs support.

claims.text: The gap is caused by a hierarchy mismatch: upgraded Smart+ campaigns have four levels of reporting, while MMPs support only three levels of campaign structure.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

claims.text: Because the MMP model has only three levels, the ad level of the Smart+ structure has no MMP-side counterpart, so its name and data cannot be carried into MMP reporting.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

conditions: Inferred from the documented 4-vs-3 mismatch plus the documented absence of ad-level data on MMPs; the packet does not state an explicit level-by-level mapping.

sections.summary: The packet documents only the limitation and its cause; it describes no usage scenarios, workflows, or advertiser cases, so no use cases can be stated.
The evidence describes a structural non-support with no menus, settings, or configuration steps, so no setup path is documented or reconstructed here.

The packet names no metrics or KPI guidance; its only measurement statement is that ad-level name and data are absent from MMP reporting, so which KPIs remain visible on the MMP side cannot be characterised.
Answered by the relationships list: the packet documents a structural non-equivalence between upgraded Smart+ reporting and MMP reporting, not a substitute feature.

claims.text: MMP reporting of upgraded Smart+ campaigns is not equivalent to Smart+ in-platform reporting: MMPs support three levels of campaign structure while upgraded Smart+ has four, so the ad level is missing on the MMP side.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

sections.summary: One official TikTok Ads help-centre source backs the packet; the packet carries no check date, so none is stated here.

claims.text: The sole evidence source for this guide is TikTok's official Ads help article on reporting for the upgraded Smart+ experience (source_id: tiktok.smart_plus.reporting), at the URL given in the evidence reference.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)

relationships.name: MMP reporting of upgraded Smart+ campaigns
relationships.difference: MMPs support only three levels of campaign structure against upgraded Smart+'s four reporting levels, so the ad-level name and data are not reported on MMPs; Smart+ in-platform reporting retains all four levels.
relationships.context: When upgraded Smart+ campaign results are consolidated through an MMP dashboard, the Smart+ ad level has no counterpart in the MMP's three-level structure.

evidence.locator: Explanation of ad-level non-reporting on MMPs (4-level Smart+ structure vs 3-level MMP support)
